title: Harvey Mobile with Voice for iOS and Android
format_note: 19 s mobile-app teaser: tagline, phone opens, one dictated legal question and its answer, 'Coming Soon' with store badges, brand line.
one_thing: You can ask Harvey a legal question by voice on your phone and get a cited answer; the apps are coming soon.

transcript.voice_style: No narrator. The only speech is the product's dictated user query, a neutral spoken question, one segment at 0-10.2 s per whisper.
transcript.script_shape: Tagline, then a single question typed as it is spoken, then the answer, then two short claim lines and a brand line. All meaning is carried by on-screen text.

structure.frame0: Off-white ground with a pale grey 'Harvey' wordmark mid-fade, left of centre; nothing else (f0001.jpg). Metrics flag it not-evidence.
structure.first_3s: Wordmark at 0-1.0 s; 'Legal Work, On the Move.' assembles word by word 1.04-1.25 s and holds to ~2.3 s; fades out and a grey phone appears at 2.5 s (strips/window-01, window-02).

beats.what: Pale 'Harvey' wordmark fades in on off-white ground.
'Legal Work, On the Move.' appears word by word, then fades.
Black phone with serif H splash, wakes to a white Harvey home screen between 3.3 and 3.7 s.
Camera pushes into the 'Ask Harvey anything' bar with plus, wand and mic icons.
Voice dictation: purple stop button and waveform dots, question typed word by word, grey word trailing.
Card zooms back out into a phone as the question is sent; spinner on the purple button.
Answer screen: 13 Australian Privacy Principles listed, cited to Schedule 1 of the Privacy Act 1988.
'Coming Soon' with App Store and Google Play badges.
'AI Tailored for Law' with small 'Harvey' wordmark below.

hero_moment.what: The answer screen fills the phone: bold '13 Australian Privacy Principles' and a numbered list, the film's one concrete fact (f0007.jpg).

ending.cta_text: Coming Soon (App Store, Google Play badges); AI Tailored for Law
ending.what: Availability line with two store badges, then a final brand line with the wordmark, held to the last frame.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: One hard cut at 2.5 s; every other seam is a fade or a scale move. A 5.71 s hold (t=4.875) carries the dictation; later holds run 1.08-2.29 s (events.json holds). No burst.

look.ground: Flat off-white (luma 246.2, saturation 0.001) filling every frame; no gradient or texture.
palette: single purple #5B3FA6-ish accent on the stop button and waveform
look.accent_use: Purple appears only on the recording stop button and waveform dots (f0004, f0005) and the send spinner (f0006); everything else is monochrome.
look.type: Large high-contrast serif for all headlines and the wordmark; neutral grotesque inside the app UI. One size per card, centred, no bold or colour changes in headlines.
look.depth: Flat; the phone has a soft drop shadow and a faint ghost outline while zooming (strips/window-04), otherwise no layers or parallax.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Push-in from phone to the input bar at 4.3-5.0 s, a flat card for the dictation 5-10 s, then a pull-back to the full phone at 10.5-11.2 s.
product_ui.notes: Input card and its icons read cleanly (crops/askbar.png, crops/voice.png). The answer screen, with the phone only 210 px wide, is legible at 1280 px but body text is about 1 % of frame height (crops/phone-answer.png).

motion.text_entry: Headline words fade in one after another within ~0.2 s (1.04-1.25 s); later titles fade up from pale grey to black over ~0.3 s (13.8-14.17 s); the typed query grows word by word with the newest word grey.
motion.ui_motion: Phone screen fades black to white in 0.5 s (3.2-3.7 s); waveform dots swell into bars during speech; purple button becomes a spinner on send.
motion.camera: Scale moves only: push into the input bar at 4.7-4.96 s, pull back to the phone at 10.6-11.2 s, phone shrinks and fades at 13.5-13.9 s.
motion.eases: Soft ease-in-out on all fades and scales; no overshoot or bounce seen in strips.

good.observation: One idea per card, centred on a flat ground, with a single accent colour reserved for the recording state. The eye never has to choose.
The feature is shown working with a real-sounding legal question: dictation, send, answer. The viewer sees the outcome, not a claim.
Headline type is large and consistent, 6.9-8.9 % of frame height, one line, at most 5 words.
Scale moves, not cuts, join the phone and the input card: push in at 4.7 s and pull back at 10.6 s keep the same object on screen.
The ending stacks three short statements in the same place and size: claim, availability with store badges, brand line.
The dictation card shows input state clearly: mic icon becomes purple stop button, dotted bar becomes a waveform, grey trailing word.

weak.observation: The tagline is held about 1.1 s for five words, below the 2 s the reading rule asks for, and it then fades with no time to re-read.
The answer screen is a 210 px-wide phone on a 1280 px frame, so list text is about 1 % of frame height; on a phone playback it would not be readable.
Large empty ground on both sides of the phone for 2.5-14 s; the phone is 16 % of frame width.
Peak level is -0.1 dBTP, above the -1 dBTP ceiling, at -13.3 LUFS.

rule_candidates.rule: A faint lone wordmark at frame 0 can work if the claim headline is fully legible by 1.3 s and the first product frame arrives by 2.5 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001.jpg wordmark; strip window-01 headline complete at 1.25 s; phone at 2.5 s.

rule_candidates.rule: Show the feature end to end in one held take: input, state change, send, answer, with the answer's key fact (a number or named source) readable on screen.
rule_candidates.evidence: Typed question 5-10 s, answer with '13 Australian Privacy Principles' at 12 s (f0007.jpg, crops/phone-answer.png).

rule_candidates.rule: In a sparse product teaser, link scenes with scale moves of one object (push-in, pull-back, 0.3-0.7 s) rather than cuts; one hard cut in 19 s is enough.
rule_candidates.evidence: metrics hard_cuts 1; strips window-04 (4.7-4.96 s), window-06 (10.6-11.2 s).

rule_candidates.rule: Reserve one accent colour for the live-interaction state (record, send); keep all else monochrome so the state change is the loudest thing in the frame.
rule_candidates.evidence: Purple only at crops/voice.png stop button and waveform; saturation 0.001.

rule_candidates.rule: A soft film may use equal-length fades for headline entrance and exit (~0.3 s each) when each headline sits alone on an empty ground.
rule_candidates.evidence: 'Work Without Boundaries' in 13.83-14.17 s, out 15.08-15.4 s (strips window-07, window-08).

rule_candidates.rule: End with three stacked cards at the same centre and size: benefit line, availability plus store badges, brand line; give each 1.1-1.8 s and the last at least 2 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: Cards at 14.1, 15.7, 17.3 s; heights 6.9-8.9 % (title_measurements); last held 1.83 s.

rule_candidates.rule: A product film can run on a near-empty off-white ground with the subject filling 60-68 % of frame height and nothing else on screen.
rule_candidates.evidence: Phone 92-582 px of 720 in f0006.jpg; whitespace both sides across 2.5-14 s.

rule_candidates.rule: Keep true peak at or below -1 dBTP; this reference reaches -0.1 dBTP at -13.3 LUFS, which is a clipping risk after lossy encoding.
